rawOrder('id','asc') inspected: emits `(id IS NULL) ASC, id ASC, id DESC`. The trailing `id DESC` is redundant when `id ASC` already precedes it, but `id` is the unique, non-null PK so the tiebreaker is never reached â€” harmless, reported as Minor below (matches the prompt's guidance).

CROSS-TASK OBSERVATION (not an in-scope T9 defect): the spec's product summary breakdown `{total, out_of_stock}` is NOT returned by this endpoint. strengths: Additive-only diff: the legacy contract (supplier filter, search, id-ASC default, hard cap 100, top-level `data` array) is preserved exactly; `meta` is purely additive, which is the correct discipline for a shared public marketplace/catalog endpoint.

Correct reuse of the shared ListQuery helper (App\Support\ListQuery, created by T1) â€” resolveSort with an explicit caller default ('id','asc') instead of the global created_at DESC, and rawOrder for portable nulls-last ordering.

meta.total is computed from a clone taken BEFORE order/limit/offset and from the SAME filtered builder (applyCatalogFilters applied first), so it reflects search + supplier eligibility and is never the page length â€” verified end-to-end (150 rows â†’ total 150 vs data 100; search=P00 â†’ total 9).
Defensive scalarQueryString() guard applied uniformly to sort/order/cursor/limit; the allowlist means no user string can reach raw SQL â€” no injection surface.
index() at 30 lines with four focused, well-named, well-commented helpers; clear separation between filter application, limit resolution, sort resolution, and scalar reads.
Tests are non-vacuous and purpose-built (divergent id vs created_at ordering to distinguish the products default from the global default; NULL created_at row to assert nulls-last).
Constants instead of magic values: SORT_ALLOWLIST and DEFAULT_LIMIT are named class constants.

issues.description: Redundant ORDER BY term: ListQuery::rawOrder('id','asc') yields `(id IS NULL) ASC, id ASC, id DESC`. For the default sort the trailing `id DESC` tiebreaker is unreachable because `id` is the unique, non-null primary key, and even for other allowlist columns the tiebreak is redundant whenever the resolved column is `id`. Harmless (deterministic ordering, no correctness impact, id is never NULL) â€” the helper is shared/out-of-scope for T9 and already unit-tested, so no change requested.

Duplication debt: `scalarQueryString(Request,string,string)` is now byte-identical (md5-verified) across 5 controllers of this plan â€” AdminOutletController.php:117, OrderController.php:126, ProductController.php:115, PromotionController.php:114, UserRoleController.php:121. T9 added the 5th copy, so the '3+ identical logic' heuristic is nominally met. Classified Minor (not Important) for consistency with the T6 (2 copies) and T7 (3 copies) auditors, and because: (a) it is a 5-line defensive input-guard boilerplate, while the drift-prone logic is centralized in ListQuery; (b) the plan's architecture deliberately uses per-controller wiring; (c) fixing it inside T9 would require editing 4 already-approved out-of-scope controllers, which T9's file scope forbids. Recommend a dedicated consolidation follow-up (e.g. a small trait/base controller or ListQuery::scalarString) rather than a T9 fix.

Test coverage gap: no test exercises a NON-ZERO offset cursor or an explicit `limit` for this endpoint (no `?limit=â€¦&cursor=â€¦` case asserting the second page / has_more=true). Offset semantics and the limit clamp are verified here only by code read + an independent probe (limit=5&cursor=5 â†’ ids 6..10; limit=200â†’100; limit=0â†’1), not by a ProductTest assertion. The array test `?cursor[]=5` only proves scalar-safety, not positive-offset paging. Same gap the T6 auditor noted for the users endpoint; a page-2 test would close it.

PRE-EXISTING (not introduced by T9), out of the T9 scalar-safety contract: `?search[]=x` still 500s because `Product::scopeSearch(?string $search)` type-hints string and `$request->query('search')` is passed straight through (ProductController.php:70). Verified: passing an array raises `TypeError: scopeSearch(): Argument #2 must be of type ?string, array given`. This behaviour is identical to the parent (29b0fc2) and the T9 contract only lists sort/order/cursor as required scalar-safe params, so it is not a T9 defect â€” noted for completeness only.
